stem:
Hydrogen peroxide is a liquid at $298\text{ K}$. It is moderately stable under room conditions but will decompose quickly if a catalyst is added.

reaction 1 $$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{l}) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g})$$

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Predict the sign of the standard entropy change of reaction 1.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Some bond energy data are shown in Table 3.1.

Table 3.1

| type of bond | bond energy / $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{O}-\text{O}$ | 150 |
| $\text{O}-\text{H}$ | 460 |
| $\text{O}=\text{O}$ | 496 |

Use the data in Table 3.1 to show that the enthalpy change of the following reaction is $-196\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g})$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Some standard entropies, $S^\ominus$, are shown in Table 3.2.

Table 3.2

| substance | $S^\ominus$ / $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{l})$ | +102 |
| $\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ | +70 |

The enthalpy change and Gibbs free energy change for the following reaction are shown.

$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{l}) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \quad \Delta H^\ominus = -196\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \quad \Delta G^\ominus = -238\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Use the data given to calculate the standard entropy of oxygen, $S^\ominus$, $\text{O}_2(\text{g})$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The decomposition of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(\text{aq})$ is catalysed by aqueous iron(III) chloride and by silver metal.

Identify which of these two catalysts is acting as a homogeneous catalyst.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
The $E^\ominus$ values for two electrode reactions are given.

$$\text{Cr}^{3+} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Cr}^{2+} \quad E^\ominus = -0.41\text{ V}$$

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
An electrochemical cell is constructed with the following half-cells (electrodes):

- an acidified solution of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, a platinum wire
- $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ mixed with $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, a platinum wire.

Identify the positive half-cell and calculate the standard cell potential, $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the value of $\Delta G^\ominus$ for the cell reaction that occurs, per mole of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem:
$$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \quad E^\ominus = +1.77\text{ V}$$
$$\text{Co}^{3+} + \text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Co}^{2+} \quad E^\ominus = +1.82\text{ V}$$

An electrochemical cell is constructed with the following half-cells.

half-cell 1 an acidified solution of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ under standard conditions, a platinum wire

half-cell 2 a solution containing $0.020\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Co}^{3+}$ and $2.0\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{Co}^{2+}$, a platinum wire

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.text: Use the Nernst equation to calculate the value of $E$, the electrode potential of half-cell 2 under these conditions.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the cell reaction that occurs in this cell under these conditions.

parts.label: (g)(i)
parts.text: Define enthalpy change of hydration, $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}$.

parts.label: (g)(ii)
parts.text:
Aluminium fluoride, $\text{AlF}_3$, is an ionic solid.

Complete and label the energy cycle to show the relationship between:

- the enthalpy change of solution of $\text{AlF}_3$, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{sol}}$
- the lattice energy of $\text{AlF}_3$, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{latt}}$
- the enthalpy changes of hydration of $\text{Al}^{3+}$ and $\text{F}^-$, $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{hyd}}$.

Include state symbols for all substances and ions.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (g)(iii)
parts.text:
Relevant data for this question are given.

$$\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{sol}} \text{AlF}_3 = -209\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{hyd}} \text{Al}^{3+} = -4690\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{hyd}} \text{F}^- = -506\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Use these data and your energy cycle in (g)(ii) to calculate the $\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{latt}}$ of $\text{AlF}_3$.
